masthead.title: web4u index
masthead.abstract: A working index of eighteen projects shared in the room #resources — solar-powered magazines, clay circuit boards, potato networks, compost servers, and a retired webring. Filed here as an archive: a list of links, lightly annotated. Computing that asks for less and lasts longer.

sections.title: Principles & Theory
sections.desc: Texts and frameworks that argue for a different relationship to computation.

sections.title: Practice & Hardware
sections.desc: Objects, devices and tutorials — energy and matter made visible.

sections.title: Networks & Tools
sections.desc: Webrings, slow protocols, and the small utilities that hold the scene together.

links.title: Low-Tech Magazine
links.desc: A solar-powered website that goes offline when its battery runs low, and dithers every image to save energy.

links.title: Lo—TEK: Design by Radical Indigenism
links.desc: Julia Watson's book on nature-based technologies rooted in Traditional Ecological Knowledge.

links.title: Indigenous Groups & Their Own ChatGPT
links.desc: Atmos on Tainá — an Amazon-built AI vault, stored locally, owned by the community.

links.title: Lo-TEK Institute
links.desc: The Lo-TEK movement's Instagram. External link only — not archived here.

links.title: Permacomputing
links.desc: Devine Lu Linvega's wiki: frugal, salvage and collapse computing; design for disassembly.

links.title: Newton Machine Manifesto
links.desc: Reconstrained Design's ten-point manifesto for community-built gravity batteries that store energy as story.

links.title: The Potato Internet
links.desc: Caroline Sinders' anti-upscaling social network, partly powered by potatoes and e-waste.

links.title: Clay PCB Tutorial
links.desc: Feminist Hackerspaces make printed circuit boards from wild clay and urban-mined silver.

links.title: Open Source Salt Battery
links.desc: Shashwath Santosh's battery, built entirely from found objects and scrap metal.

links.title: Cardboard Computer
links.desc: Zach Rotholz's flat-pack corrugated laptop for kids, built around a Raspberry Pi.

links.title: Zonneliedjes
links.desc: Gieskes: songs made directly from sunlight on circuit-bent, solar-powered instruments.

links.title: ASH — AI Pocket Field Guide
links.desc: A real-life Pokédex for young 'ecology guardians,' running iNaturalist on a Coral board.

links.title: Compost Computer
links.desc: FutureEverything & UAL: a web server powered by the bio-energy of a community compost heap.

links.title: Onionring
links.desc: Allium House's tiny JavaScript widget for building webrings with almost no technical knowledge.

links.title: Low Tech Webring
links.desc: Em Reed's (retired) webring for Web 1.0-inspired, low-tech homepages. The spiritual hub.

links.title: Slow Net
links.desc: Beverly Chou's experiments in deliberate slowness as resistance to data extraction.

links.title: Fit on a Floppy
links.desc: Checks whether your webpage fits on a 1.44MB floppy. A physical reminder of filesize.

links.title: Dither it!
links.desc: Free in-browser image dithering — Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson, Bayer. Processed locally.

links.title: Tooooools.app
links.desc: Lo-fi image and video effects: dithering, halftone, CRT, ASCII. Free, no sign-up.

colophon.blurb: An index assembled from links shared in #resources. No trackers, no cookies. The field above is generated live in WebGL — slate with a single electric-violet accent — and pauses when the tab is hidden.
